title: Solar Rebates in Vaughan 2026: Newer Roofs and Up to $10,000
desc: Vaughan solar rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: the youngest housing in our Ontario data, 86% ownership and Alectra as the utility.
badge: Up to $10,000 for solar and battery
lead: Vaughan has 65,040 detached households, 86% of households own and only 8% of homes predate 1981. Solar suits a newer roof, so this may be Vaughan's best fit among the program's upgrades.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for solar and batteries in Vaughan
cards_intro: We re-read the program's solar page and its October 2025 requirements on October 3, 2026. The rebate comes with conditions that change how the system is designed, so read them before you ask for quotes.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: Paid on installed DC capacity, capped at 50% of eligible costs. Rooftop systems only, including a garage roof on the same meter.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Only with a new solar system, also capped at 50% of eligible costs. Combined solar and battery rebates reach $10,000.

cards.title: No net metering
cards.amount: Rebate excluded if you net meter
cards.note: A system under an Ontario net metering agreement is not eligible. The system must be sized for load displacement only.

cards.title: Approvals before you buy
cards.note: The contractor files the pre-installation application with a quote dated within 60 days. You cannot buy or install before IESO pre-approval and your local utility's approval.

cards.title: Finish within 12 months
cards.note: The project must be complete within 12 months of approval, with the ESA certificate and the connection agreement filed within 30 days of installation.

cards.title: First-time installs only
cards.note: Homes that already have solar or storage are not eligible. Leases, rentals and lease-to-own arrangements are excluded.

after_cards: The requirements document gives no end date for this stream, and funding conditions can change, so confirm on the program page before you sign. The IESO has no pre-qualified contractor list for it.
sections: A strong case for solar here

With a young housing stock, a low major-repairs rate (2.5%) and high ownership, Vaughan has many roofs that are good candidates. The insulation rebates may have little to pay for here, since a newer attic may sit above the program's tables, which makes solar and heat pumps the more relevant upgrades.
Alectra approves the connection and the contractor must attest that the generation connection application will be filed. The program recommends discussing maximum capacity with the utility first.

Vaughan gets about 3.83 peak sun hours a day. The program wants the system sized to offset the home's consumption, not to export. Ask for the proposed annual output next to your last twelve months of bills.

Many Ontario solar quotes assume net metering, where extra power sent to the grid earns bill credits. This program does not allow it: a system under a net metering agreement is not eligible, and the system must be sized for load displacement, meaning it should match what the home uses. A Vaughan owner who wants the rebate should tell every installer up front, because a system designed to export will not qualify.

The panels must be on the roof of the house or of a permanent structure on the same property and connected to the home's meter, such as a detached garage. Ground mounts are not eligible, and neither are systems on trailers or other temporary structures. Vaughan has 65,040 detached houses, where roof orientation and shading decide the system size.

The order matters. The contractor submits the pre-installation application with a quote dated within 60 days, you receive written pre-approval and your utility's approval, and only then do you buy and install. The system must be finished within 12 months of approval, and the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days of installation.

You must own the home and be the person paying for the system. A tenant cannot apply for the owner. In Vaughan, 14% of households rent, and only eligible house types qualify: single detached, semi-detached, row, townhome or mobile home on a permanent foundation.
claim_steps: Confirm you own an eligible house type with a roof or garage that suits panels.
Talk to Alectra Utilities about the connection process and the maximum system size allowed before you sign anything.
Choose a licensed electrical contractor and ask for a quote that shows the DC capacity in kW and the eligible costs without HST.
Let the contractor file the pre-installation application, and wait for written IESO pre-approval and utility approval before buying or installing.
After the install, check that the post-installation application is filed within 30 days with the ESA certificate and connection agreement.
faq: Is solar a good fit for newer homes?
Newer roofs are generally an advantage.
To offset the home's own use.
